author: IGN
description:
In today's Daily Fix: The Batman Part 2 has stopped production as director Matt Reeves has stepped away for personal reasons. DC Studios and Warner Bros. have confirmed to Deadline that Reeves is focusing on a "family matter," and there is no timeline yet for his return. In other news, Capcom has revealed plans to convert their in-house RE Engine into an AI-generation game engine. Programmer Satoshi Ishida said that the focus is on streamlining certain aspects of development, not to create assets wholesale. The RE Engine has powered several of Capcom's latest hits including Resident Evil Requiem, Pragmata, and Monster Hunter Wilds. And finally, we're previewing Mine Cart Madness from inside SUper Nintendo World with The Ride Guys at Universal Epic Universe at Universal Orlando Resort.

Presented by Universal Orlando Resort and its newest theme park, Universal Epic Universe.
title: The Batman 2 Halts Production as Director Matt Reeves Steps Away - IGN Daily Fix

author: IGN
description:
How long could you survive inside the belly of a whale? 

In the upcoming survival thriller, Whalefall, Austin Abrams plays Jay Gardiner, a scuba diver searching off the California coast for the remains of his late father, played by Josh Brolin. But after being swallowed by a massive sperm whale, Jay has just one hour of oxygen to escape, forcing him to rely on the lessons his father taught him in a tense, claustrophobic race for survival. So naturally, to find out what this would feel like, we built a set that shrinks to approximately the size of a whale's stomach. To simulate the pressure of running out of oxygen, IGN’s Jeffrey Vega must attempt to survive in Subnautica 2 as the walls close in around him.

Presented by 20th Century Studios’ Whalefall. Only in theaters on October 16th.
title: I Built a Room That Crushes Me While I Play Subnautica 2

author: IGN
description:
So, you’re thinking about buying a PS5 for GTA 6? Well, it turns out there are plenty of other great games to play on Sony’s latest console once you tear yourself away from the streets of Leonida. From sprawling RPGs to terrifying survival horror, there’s just as strong a variety of fantastic experiences today as there was when we first visited Vice City back on the PlayStation 2. 

Gaming has changed a lot since the days of memory cards and CRT, though, and we’re in an era of cross-generational updates and remasters. So when we began our search for the very best PlayStation 5 games, we set ourselves one important rule: they had to be _genuine_ PS5 games. The first time these games arrived on a Sony console, it had to be the PS5. No remasters, ports, backwards compatibility, or upgrades here. Remakes created for this generation, of course, are welcome. 

So, what are those games? Well, let me tell you. These are the 25 best PS5 games.
title: Top 25 Best PS5 Games

description:
In Insidious: Out of the Further, Amelia Eve stars as Gemma, a young mother raising her daughter in the house she grew up in, who discovers she can travel into The Further, the purgatorial realm of lost souls at the heart of the Insidious universe. 

When something evil comes after her, Gemma discovers an ability that changes everything; she doesn’t just enter The Further, she can bring what lives there back to the real world. Once the demons realize her power, our world becomes their playground.

Insidious: Out of the Further is available on digital October 6 and on Blu-ray and DVD December 1.
